# docker_node (Resource)

Manages the labels, availability and role of a swarm node that has already joined, like `docker node update`, through the provider's Docker host (which must be a manager). It never joins or leaves: use `docker_swarm_node` to join a host. Destroying the resource only removes it from Terraform state; the node stays in the swarm with its current labels, availability and role.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Manage a node that already joined the swarm (for example with
# `docker swarm join` outside Terraform). The provider must point at a
# manager. Destroying this resource only forgets the node: it stays in the
# swarm with its current labels, availability and role.
resource "docker_node" "worker1" {
  node_id      = "worker1" # node ID or hostname
  name         = "edge-worker-1"
  availability = "active"
  labels = {
    zone = "a"
    disk = "ssd"
  }
}

output "worker1_addr" {
  value = docker_node.worker1.addr
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `node_id` (String) The node to manage: ID, unique ID prefix, hostname or node name (resolved to the node ID, see `id`). Forces replacement.

### Optional

- `availability` (String) Scheduling availability: `active`, `pause` or `drain` (`Spec.Availability`). Unset leaves it as it is. Updated in place (NodeUpdate); draining does not wait for tasks to leave (use `docker_node_drain` for that).
- `labels` (Map of String) Node labels (`Spec.Labels`, `node.labels.*` in placement constraints). When set, the node gets exactly these labels (others are removed); unset leaves them as they are. Updated in place.
- `name` (String) Node name (`Spec.Name`), else the hostname. Set it to name the node (`NodeSpec.Name`); unset leaves the node's name as it is. Updated in place (NodeUpdate).
- `role` (String) Node role: `worker` or `manager` (`Spec.Role`). Unset leaves it as it is. Updated in place (promote / demote); the Engine refuses to demote the last manager.

### Read-Only

- `addr` (String) IP address the node is reached at (`Status.Addr`).
- `content_sha256` (String) SHA-256 of inspect_json; changes whenever the object changes.
- `docker_server_version` (String) Docker Engine version of the daemon the provider talked to (GET /version Version).
- `engine_api_version` (String) Engine API version the provider negotiated with the daemon (GET /version ApiVersion, capped by the client's max).
- `hostname` (String) Hostname the node reports (`Description.Hostname`).
- `id` (String) Full node ID. This is the import ID (a hostname works too).
- `inspect` (Attributes) The node inspect response as a nested object mirroring Node field by field (snake_case). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--inspect))
- `inspect_json` (String) The exact Engine API inspect response for the node, as JSON.
- `version_index` (Number) The node object's `Version.Index`; it changes on every update of the node.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the node ID or its hostname.
terraform import docker_node.worker1 worker1
```
